title: The three types of machine learning
intro: Three families: supervised (learning with answers), unsupervised (structure without labels) and reinforcement (learning via reward).
keyPoints: Supervised learning: learning with labels — classification (category) and regression (number). This course's focus.
Unsupervised learning: finding structure without labels — clustering, PCA, anomaly detection.
Reinforcement learning: learning by trial-and-error with rewards (no fixed labels).
Two questions pick the family: do you have labels? and are you predicting a number or a category?

blocks.html: Classified by feedback type: examples with answers = supervised; data only, finding structure = unsupervised; learning by acting and earning rewards = reinforcement.
Supervised is by far the most common — exactly what scikit-learn means by “fit on (X, y)”.

sections.title: Supervised learning: learning with the answer attached

blocks.html: Data consists of pairs: features X (what you know) and target y (the answer). The model learns the map X → y so it can predict y for new X.

rows: MSE, RMSE, MAE, R² — see the Evaluation & metrics chapter

blocks.html: Two classes is binary, three or more multi-class. Note: despite its name, logistic regression is classification.
Hallmark of supervised learning: you already have the answer for the training data; the model is tested on questions it has not seen.
Without labels, unsupervised learning looks for structure: clustering (KMeans), dimensionality reduction (PCA), anomaly detection. Example: customer segmentation.
Eight points, two clusters: KMeans finds them without anyone naming the groups. Run the code yourself.

blocks.caption: KMeans finds structure without labels
blocks.source:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

# 8 points in 2D — two visible groups
X = np.array([[1, 2], [1.5, 1.8], [1.2, 2.2],
              [8, 9], [8.5, 8.8], [8.2, 9.3],
              [1.1, 1.9], [8.8, 9.1]])

km = KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=10, random_state=0).fit(X)
print('cluster per point :', km.labels_)
print('centres           :', km.cluster_centers_.round(1))
print('point [2, 2]      -> cluster', km.predict([[2, 2]])[0],
      '(belongs to the bottom-left group)')

blocks.html: There is no y to check against: you judge clustering quality yourself, by interpretation.
An agent learns by acting: actions yield (delayed) reward or punishment; the policy maximizes total reward. Uses: robotics, game AI, RLHF.
Difference with supervised: there you get the correct answer per example; here you must discover which actions led to the reward — often much later.

rows: “I have examples with the correct answer.”
“I only have data and am looking for structure or groups.”

blocks.html: Two questions place any system: do you have labels? And does feedback arrive per example or via reward?
